agent_diagnosis_message.content:
# Task overview
On branch `still-omega`, `/book?broken=1` blocks keyboard-only slot selection (WCAG 2.1 SC 2.1.1), while `/simple` works. The task was to diagnose this and give the minimal repair diff for `apps/web/components/booking-flow.tsx`.

# External resources
- Issue #1 in project 88027269 (`vaibhav.lalwani/still#1`) reports that the slot radio gets `tabIndex={brokenPrimary ? -1 : undefined}` when `brokenPrimary` is active, so Tab and arrow keys can't reach the slots. A Duo root-cause note on the issue confirms this.
- Issue #1 in project 88027224 is a mirror of the same bug. Neither issue has a linked MR.

# Code exploration
Only two files matter: `apps/web/components/booking-flow.tsx` and `apps/web/components/booking-page.tsx`. A repo-wide grep found no other use of `brokenPrimary`, `tabIndex` or `broken=1`.

`booking-page.tsx` renders `<BookingFlow simpleMode={simple} />`. `/simple` passes `simpleMode=true` and the primary route passes `false`.

In `booking-flow.tsx`, a `useEffect` sets `brokenPrimary` to true only when `!simpleMode` and the URL has `?broken=1`. In `/simple` the flag stays `false`, so `/simple` never gets the defect.

The defect is on the slot radio inside the `role="radiogroup"` slot list (around line 330):
```tsx
<input
  checked={selectedSlot === slot.id}
  name="slot"
  onChange={() => setSelectedSlot(slot.id)}
  tabIndex={brokenPrimary ? -1 : undefined}
  type="radio"
  value={slot.id}
/>
```

Root cause: `tabIndex={-1}` removes the native radios from the sequential focus order. Tab skips the group and arrow keys never apply. The submit button stays disabled because `!selectedSlot`, so the booking journey is blocked. With `tabIndex={undefined}`, native radio-group behaviour applies: one Tab stop, then arrow keys move focus and selection.

A banner (`className="journey-warning"`) is also shown when `brokenPrimary` is true. It tells users that keyboard navigation is disabled.

# Architectural Context
`BookingFlow` is a Next.js client component that uses `@/lib/api` and `./icons`. `BookingPage` mounts it for both routes. `?broken=1` is a deliberate demo regression that triggers STILL's fallback flow. The scripts and `/health` endpoint mentioned in the Duo comment are not in this checkout, so I did not inspect them.

# Related Patterns
The other form controls in the same file (`#service`, `#name`, `#email`) set no `tabIndex`. That is the pattern the slot radio should follow.

# Implementation Guidance
Minimal repair diff:
```diff
--- a/apps/web/components/booking-flow.tsx
+++ b/apps/web/components/booking-flow.tsx
@@ -330,7 +330,6 @@ export function BookingFlow({ simpleMode }: { simpleMode: boolean }) {
                         checked={selectedSlot === slot.id}
                         name="slot"
                         onChange={() => setSelectedSlot(slot.id)}
-                        tabIndex={brokenPrimary ? -1 : undefined}
                         type="radio"
                         value={slot.id}
                       />
```
This restores native keyboard behaviour. `brokenPrimary` is still used by the banner, so there is no unused-variable lint error, and nothing else depends on `tabIndex`.

Optional follow-ups:
- Remove or reword the `journey-warning` banner, which now falsely claims keyboard navigation is disabled.
- Do not replace `-1` with `0`. An explicit `tabIndex={0}` on every radio would make each radio its own Tab stop and break the native single-tab-stop radio-group pattern.
- Validate outside this file as the issue requests: Tab into the radiogroup, arrow-key selection, an axe scan, and a Playwright keyboard-selection test. I did not locate the existing test directories.
